Definition: to subside; by implication, to be overflowed, cease; causatively, to abate, subdue
BiblicalUsage: Waters subside when God speaks, and a fire is quenched when Moses prays. Amos says the land shall rise up wholly as a flood, and be cast out and drowned, and Ezekiel promises that God will make the waters deep and cause the rivers to run like oil. The people cried unto Moses, and when Moses prayed unto the LORD, the fire was quenched.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God quiets the waters He raised, and the fire He kindled goes out at the prayer of one man.
